questions.text: Walk me through how you took a model from a notebook to a production service. What did you change along the way?

follow_up_suggestions.text: How did you package the model, and how did you test the serving code?
How did you confirm the production model matched the offline results?

scoring_rubric.1: Cannot describe moving a model to production
scoring_rubric.2: Describes deployment without changes for production
scoring_rubric.3: Refactors code, versions the model and tests serving
scoring_rubric.4: Checks parity between offline and online behaviour and plans rollback
scoring_rubric.5: Also explains latency, cost trade-offs and the release process for models

questions.text: How do you detect that a production model has degraded, and what do you do when it has?

follow_up_suggestions.text: Which signals do you monitor, such as inputs, predictions or outcomes?
How do you decide between retraining and rolling back?

scoring_rubric.2: Monitors system health only, not model quality
scoring_rubric.3: Tracks input drift and prediction distributions
scoring_rubric.4: Uses outcome metrics with alert thresholds and a response plan
scoring_rubric.5: Also explains feedback loops, labelling delays and governance of retraining

questions.text: How do you make a training pipeline reproducible, so that another engineer can rerun last quarter's model?

follow_up_suggestions.text: What exactly do you record for each training run?
How do you handle data that changes after training?

scoring_rubric.2: Saves the code but not data, parameters or environment
scoring_rubric.3: Tracks code version, parameters and dataset version
scoring_rubric.4: Pins environments and records metrics and artefacts for every run
scoring_rubric.5: Also explains data snapshots, lineage and automated re-runs

questions.text: A model's latency doubled after a release. How would you investigate?

follow_up_suggestions.text: Where in the serving path would you measure first?
How would you reduce latency without changing predictions?

scoring_rubric.2: Guesses the model is the cause without evidence
scoring_rubric.3: Profiles the serving path to find the slow step
scoring_rubric.4: Separates model, feature and infrastructure causes and fixes the right one
scoring_rubric.5: Also proves predictions are unchanged after the fix and adds a latency budget

questions.text: How do you decide whether a more complex model is worth its extra cost in production?

follow_up_suggestions.text: What baseline do you compare against, and why?
How do you explain the trade-off to a non-technical stakeholder?

scoring_rubric.1: Chooses models by default without comparison
scoring_rubric.3: Compares against a simple baseline on business metrics and cost
scoring_rubric.4: Considers latency, maintenance and risk alongside accuracy
scoring_rubric.5: Also plans a staged rollout and a clear decision record for stakeholders
